title: Selected Topics Public Policy; Race and Public Policy
description:
For PLCY majors or permission of instructor.

The changing definitions of race in America have been shaped by political institutions for centuries. Since the founding, American institutions have been marked by racial inequality. Because of this persistent reality, politics and race continue to be intertwined. This course explores the various ways in which race and politics intersect (and possibly collide). We will observe how racial inequality - and the efforts to overcome it- affect various facets of American local, state, and national politics. Often, Prince George's County will be the launching point for broader discussions and analyses pertaining to relationships between racial and ethnic groups in this community. We will also pay particular attention to the causes of contemporary racial mobilization and to its consequences. In particular, we will discuss how Prince George's County is affected by former executives as well as the current governor and president and the remnants of the racially charged nature of the previous presidential administration.
